tasks.task: Navigate to the homepage of the health blog website and check for the presence of a search bar.
tasks.expected: The homepage displays a functional search bar prominently, enabling users to input search queries.

tasks.task: Perform a search for a specific health topic using the search bar.
tasks.expected: The search results page displays articles related to the inputted health topic, with titles and short descriptions that match the search query.

tasks.task: Access a specific article from the search results and verify the presence of a comment section.
tasks.expected: The article page contains a comment section where users can read existing comments and write their own.

tasks.task: Post a comment on an article and check the comment's appearance in the comment section.
tasks.expected: The posted comment appears in the comment section immediately after submission, displaying correctly with the user's input.

tasks.task: Browse the category section to view available health topics.
tasks.expected: The categories are clearly listed, allowing the user to select and view articles associated with each category.

tasks.task: Follow a specific health topic or category from the category list.
tasks.expected: The website confirms that the user is now following the selected topic, and it is added to a personal list or notification service.

tasks.task: Verify that the website uses 'misty rose' as the background color and 'firebrick' as the component color, as specified in the design requirements.
tasks.expected: The website has a background color of 'misty rose' and components (such as buttons, cards, headers, etc.) are styled with the color 'firebrick', accurately reflecting the design instruction.

tasks.task: On the archive page, check the Nutrition category and switch on the reviewed-only toggle.
tasks.expected: Exactly two articles remain — Understanding Gut Bacteria and Beginner's Guide to Meal Prep — and the counter reads 'Showing 2 of 8 articles'.

tasks.task: Open the archive page with no filters applied and look at the top of the list.
tasks.expected: Sleep Debt: Myth or Real? sits above Understanding Gut Bacteria — both have 3,200 views, and the newer article wins the tie.

tasks.task: On the archive page, type 5 into the maximum read time box.
tasks.expected: Only the three articles of 5 minutes or less remain visible — Hydration Myths Debunked at exactly '5 min read', 10-Minute Morning Stretch Routine, and The Science of Cold Showers.

tasks.task: From the archive, click the row for Understanding Gut Bacteria.
tasks.expected: Its full article page opens and shows the Medically Reviewed tag naming Dr. Sam Wexler.

tasks.task: Open any article and submit a comment that says 'Great tips, thanks!'.
tasks.expected: The comment appears in the article's comment section immediately after posting.

tasks.task: Take the quiz, picking the Nutrition-tagged option on questions 1 and 3, the Fitness-tagged option on questions 2 and 4, and the Sleep-tagged option on question 5.
tasks.expected: The results card names Fitness as the wellness focus — the two-two tie with Nutrition breaks toward Fitness because it was picked more recently.

tasks.task: Start the quiz and answer question 1 with a Fitness-tagged option, then pause.
tasks.expected: The running tally shows Fitness at 1 with the other topics at 0, and the progress indicator shows you are now on question 2 of 5 — all before the quiz is finished.

tasks.task: Answer question 1 with a Fitness-tagged option, click the back control, and change your answer to a Sleep-tagged option.
tasks.expected: The tally now shows Sleep at 1 and Fitness back at 0 — the old pick is removed, not double-counted.

tasks.task: Finish the quiz picking a Fitness-tagged option every time, then look at the recommended articles on the results card.
tasks.expected: The recommendations are Fitness articles listed most-viewed first — Strength Training After 50 on top — and each one shows an 'X min read' label plus its Medically Reviewed or Editorial tag.

tasks.task: Open the Nutrition discussion board.
tasks.expected: Exactly two threads show, with 'Best protein sources for vegetarians?' listed above 'Is intermittent fasting safe?' — both have 4 replies, and the newer May 2 thread wins the tie.

tasks.task: In the Fitness board, open 'Knee pain after running', type a reply saying 'Try foam rolling' and post it, then go back to the board's thread list.
tasks.expected: The reply appears in the thread and the thread's reply count in the board list now shows 2.

tasks.task: Open the Mind discussion board.
tasks.expected: Instead of a blank area, a friendly message says there's nothing here yet and nudges you to start the first thread.

tasks.task: Go to the Nutrition category page and click its link to the discussion board.
tasks.expected: You land on the Nutrition board showing its two seeded threads.

tasks.task: Type 'My knee hurts after every workout and my sleep is a mess' into the Ask the Community box.
tasks.expected: The helper routes to the Fitness board — two keyword hits (knee, workout) beat Sleep's single hit even though 'sleep' comes last — and beneath the verdict it lists Fitness's one seeded thread, 'Knee pain after running'.

tasks.task: Type 'Does stress ruin sleep?' into the Ask the Community box.
tasks.expected: The helper routes to the Mind board — the one-hit tie between Mind (stress) and Sleep (sleep) breaks toward stress because it appears first in the question — and since the Mind board has no threads yet, the duplicate-check list shows a friendly nothing-here message with a nudge rather than a blank space.

tasks.task: Slowly type 'How much protein do I need' into the Ask the Community box, watching after each keystroke.
tasks.expected: The moment the word 'protein' is completed the helper flips to the Nutrition board and lists its two seeded threads — all without pressing Enter or clicking anything.

tasks.task: Type 'Is a short nap good for sleep debt?' into the Ask the Community box, click the post button, and submit the pre-filled thread.
tasks.expected: You land on the Sleep board with the new-thread form already titled 'Is a short nap good for sleep debt?', and after submitting, the new thread sits at the top of the board above 'Can't fall asleep before 2am' — both are replyless, so the newer thread wins.

tasks.task: Open the Review Desk.
tasks.expected: The queue holds exactly four articles — Sleep Debt: Myth or Real?, Managing Stress at Work, Hydration Myths Debunked, and The Science of Cold Showers — only the Editorial ones, not all eight.

tasks.task: At the Review Desk, open Sleep Debt: Myth or Real?, tick both checklist items but leave the reviewer unpicked, and try to approve.
tasks.expected: Approval is blocked (button disabled or a clear message) until a reviewer is chosen; the article stays in the queue tagged Editorial.

tasks.task: At the Review Desk, open Managing Stress at Work and click approve, then return to the queue.
tasks.expected: The queue now holds three articles with Managing Stress at Work gone, and its article page now shows Medically Reviewed with Dr. Sam Wexler.

tasks.task: At the Review Desk, open Managing Stress at Work and click approve, then go to the archive and switch on the reviewed-only toggle.
tasks.expected: Five articles now pass the reviewed-only filter, and Managing Stress at Work is among them.

tasks.task: Open the archive page with no filters applied and look at the top of the list.

tasks.task: Open the digest composer and add every article it offers.

tasks.expected: The live summary first shows '13 min read' for the two picks, then drops to 1 pick at '4 min read' after the removal — no stale total.

tasks.task: In the digest subscribe box, type sam@wellness and submit, then change it to sam@wellness.com and submit again.
tasks.expected: The first attempt shows an inline error and no confirmation; the second shows a success confirmation.

tasks.task: At the Review Desk, open Managing Stress at Work and click approve, then open the digest composer.
